official_sources: Community Infrastructure Levy Amendment England No2 Regulations 2019
Town and Country Planning Act 1990 section 106

official_measurement_examples.name: June 2026 CIL update
official_measurement_examples.fact: National CIL guidance was updated on 17 June 2026; liability, relief, collection and reporting must retain the current charging-authority context.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning obligation legal effect
official_measurement_examples.fact: Section 106 planning obligations run with the land and are legally binding, but they are distinct from the Community Infrastructure Levy.

official_measurement_examples.name: Three statutory-policy tests
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning obligations should only support permission where they are necessary, directly related, and fairly and reasonably related in scale and kind.

official_measurement_examples.name: IFS reporting limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Infrastructure Funding Statements report secured, received, allocated and spent developer contributions; allocation is not evidence that infrastructure has already been delivered.

official_measurement_examples.name: CIL commencement distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: CIL can become due on commencement of chargeable development; a liability or demand notice is not itself planning permission or authority to commence.

official_measurement_examples.name: Relief timing
official_measurement_examples.fact: Most CIL relief or exemptions must be claimed and approved before commencement, so assumed eligibility cannot be treated as granted relief.

official_measurement_examples.name: Current appeal decisions
official_measurement_examples.fact: The national CIL appeal decisions page was updated on 16 July 2026 with a decision dated 15 July 2026; individual appeal outcomes are case-specific and not parcel-wide precedent.

official_measurement_examples.name: Contribution stack separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Section 106, section 278 highways agreements and CIL are separate contribution mechanisms and must not be silently merged into a single parcel charge.

core_rules: CIL liability is not planning permission
planning permission does not establish final CIL liability
section 106 obligation is distinct from CIL
section 278 agreement is distinct from section 106 and CIL
IFS allocation is not infrastructure delivery
historic charging schedules must retain effective dates
relief or exemption must not be assumed before formal approval
developer contribution evidence does not determine land ownership
contribution amount does not itself determine development capacity
no parcel contribution clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official GOV.UK, Planning Inspectorate and legislation.gov.uk sources checked on 2026-07-26; June-July 2026 CIL guidance and appeal updates retained with contribution-type and permission separation; no parcel promotion.
